newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks close lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks close lower on consolidation.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed lower on Monday as the market staged a consolidation in reaction to sharp rises last week, brokers said.
They said investors shied away from large-capitalised shares on weakening yen against the dollar in world markets. Foreign investors in particular took a lukewarm attitude.

"Large-capitalised shares, which led the market rises last week aided by strengthening yen, took a rest," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities. "Foreign investors are unlikely to be bolstered again on hopes for an economic turnaround."
The composite stock index fell 6.18 points to 718.99

Brokers said an agreement between the two Koreas on food aid to hunger-stricken North Korea had no impact on the market. Under the accord, South Korean Red Cross would ship 50,000 tonnes of food aid to the North by the end of July.
Despite positive factors surrounding the market, including rising customer deposits and falling interest rates, Kim said: "The future market prospects look still uncertain."

Customer deposits at brokerage houses hit a historic high of 3.3 trillion won and yields on benchmark three-year corporate bonds stood at 12.17 percent in Monday's morning, off 0.02 percentage point from the weekend.
Park Si-jin of Hanhwa Securities said corporate yields were falling as financial institutions, appearing reluctant to extend fresh loans, tended to buy only blue chip issues.
"Recent liquidity flows in the economy seemed to be distorted," Park said. "I cannot see any interest shift to the stock market from the debt market."

Banking shares were mixed after the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform proposed to expand the individual ownership ceiling in banks to 10 percent from the current four percent. Brokers said investors were studying what the commission's proposed criteria would mean for the bank ownership.
Korea First Bank lost 80 won to 3,790 and Koram Bank 8550.KS gained 400 won to 12,100.

Dainong and Jinro Group shares gained on unexpectedly strong comments by Finance and Economy Minister Kang Kyong-shik last Friday to crack down on moves by financial institutions to call in corporate debts or not to extend fresh loans with no good reason.
Both Daining Corp and Jinro went limit up, adding 210 won and 440 won to 2,930 and 5,990 respectively.
"The market will move in a boxed range of 720-730 for the time being," Park said. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
